date_note: Date is the day of the Wall Street Journal report as relayed by Reuters; the pages give no date for the attacks themselves.
title: US reportedly investigates whether Iran was behind dozens of cyberattacks on energy tankers
summary: The Wall Street Journal reported (via Reuters) that the US is investigating whether Iran was behind dozens of cyberattacks on energy tankers; as many as 50 ships are believed attacked. Russia is also seen as a possible culprit. News.az, relaying the WSJ, says a Trump administration official said no evidence directly linking Iran had been found, and the Coast Guard sent cyber teams to at least four vessels.
plain: The Wall Street Journal reports that US officials are investigating whether Iran was behind dozens of cyberattacks on tankers; as many as 50 ships are believed attacked. An administration official said no evidence directly links Iran.
exec: A WSJ report says the US is investigating whether Iran was behind attacks on as many as 50 tankers; an administration official said no evidence directly links Iran.

evidence.quote: As many as 50 ships carrying oil, liquefied petroleum, chemical products and other explosive substances

validation.note: Reuters (via WHBL) and Ynetnews both relay one Wall Street Journal report, so it is one underlying source; the WSJ original was not read. Reuters says it could not immediately verify the report; no US government statement was read. News.az also relays the same WSJ report, so it adds no independent source.

review.note: Compared title, as many as 50 ships, Iran/Russia, official no direct evidence, four Coast Guard vessels, single_source/developing against Reuters/WHBL, Ynetnews, News.az
